text:
P&G Korea, the local unit of U.S. consumer goods giant Procter & Gamble, is donating 20,000 Pampers diapers to families facing financial and social hardships, extending its support for vulnerable children and single-parent households ahead of the year-end holiday season.
The donation was made through the Salvation Army Kettle Campaign, with the diapers set to be distributed to Duri Home, a residential facility for single-parent families, other Salvation Army childcare facilities and households raising young children in need.
Duri Home provides accommodation and support for single parents raising children younger than 3, helping families establish stable living conditions while preparing for independent lives.
Alongside the donation, employees from P&G Korea's Pampers team visited Duri Home on Nov. 12 to volunteer in childcare and facility maintenance, helping create a more comfortable environment for children and their caregivers.
"Diapers are an essential everyday necessity for families raising young children, and we hope this donation will ease some of their financial burden and provide practical support for children's healthy development," said Rohini Venkateswaran, president of P&G Korea.
"P&G Korea will continue to contribute to local communities by providing support where it is needed, so that every child can grow up in a healthy and stable environment," she said.
The latest contribution builds on the company's longstanding community outreach through Pampers, which has donated more than 32,000 boxes of diapers to disadvantaged families since 2017.
Since 2018, P&G Korea has also partnered with the Kids and Future Foundation on its Family Care campaign, working to improve medical environments for pediatric patients.
Last year, Pampers employees volunteered at Seoul Medical Center following the completion of renovations to its pediatric ward, continuing the company's efforts to support children and their families beyond product donations.
